title: orders.order-revised.v1
description: A confirmed order was revised. A revision is refused once any garment has entered production (INV-JOB-02), so this event never contradicts a pinned workflow version and carries no workflow field. It carries no totals and no configuration version identifiers (Confidential; Billing reads them through IOrderSnapshotQuery and recalculates), and not the revision reason — free text a member of staff typed, which conventions.md section 5.5 does not admit and which the erasure workflow has to be able to reach. Whether the module also republishes orders.order-confirmed.v1 alongside this event is an implementation choice: that event carries revisionNumber at v1 precisely so a republication needs no new major.
$comment: additionalProperties is true on purpose. conventions.md section 5.5 permits additive changes within a major version, so a subscriber must tolerate a field it has not seen; a closed schema would make every such addition breaking. required lists the fields present when v1 was published — a field added within v1 is optional forever, because a dead-lettered message replayed later carries the payload as it was written.

eventId.description: Identity of this occurrence. Delivery is at least once; consumers de-duplicate on it.

occurredAt.description: When the revision was recorded, in UTC.

aggregateId.description: The order, so a revision is ordered against the confirmation it revises and against every later revision.

organisationId.description: The organisation the order belongs to.

branchId.description: The branch the order was taken at.

customerId.description: The customer the order is for. An identifier and nothing more.

orderNumber.description: The human reference. Unchanged by a revision: the order is the same order.

revisionId.description: The revision record this event announces — the 'on whose authority' handle, exactly the role customers.customer-merged.v1 gives its merge identifier. Who revised, when and why stays in Orders.

revisionNumber.description: The order's revision number after this change. Two or higher, because revision one is the confirmation itself.

dueDate.description: The order's promised date as at this revision, branch-local.

supersededEstimateId.description: The outstanding estimate this revision supersedes, or null where there was none.

revisedGarmentJobIds.description: Every garment the revision touched. Billing #42 must invalidate a draft invoice covering them and Reporting #45 must re-read them, which is why they are named here rather than left to a re-read of the whole order. Empty is possible — a revision may move only the order's own promised date.

schemaVersion.description: The payload's major version. Agrees with the .v suffix of eventType.
